title: George Bernard Shaw on English Spelling: The Satirical Genius of Phonetic Reform
summary: Playwright George Bernard Shaw famously demonstrated the absurdities of English orthography by inventing the spelling 'Ghoti' to be pronounced as 'Fish'.
full_text:
Throughout his long life, the celebrated Irish playwright and satirist George Bernard Shaw waged an energetic campaign against the chaotic eccentricities of English orthography.

Speaking at a London literary symposium, Shaw lamented that thousands of hours were wasted by children and second-language learners struggling with non-phonetic English spellings.

A traditionalist scholar protested:
"Mr. Shaw, our traditional orthography reflects the historical etymology of our language. There is an underlying logic to every spelling!"

Shaw smiled mischievously, picked up a piece of chalk, and scribbled five capital letters on the board:
"GHOTI"

Turning to the scholar, Shaw inquired: "How would you pronounce this word, sir?"

The scholar adjusted his spectacles: "Obviously, it is pronounced 'Go-tee'."

Shaw burst into triumphant laughter:
"Not at all, my dear professor! According to the sacred rules of English spelling, that word is pronounced 'FISH'!
Consider the evidence:
Take the 'GH' from 'enough'—pronounced 'F'!
Take the 'O' from 'women'—pronounced 'I'!
Take the 'TI' from 'nation'—pronounced 'SH'!
Put them together, and G-H-O-T-I spells F-I-S-H!"

The auditorium erupted into roaring laughter and applause. Through brilliant pedagogical humor, Shaw exposed the absurdities of archaic conventions, advocating for phonetic simplicity in education.
